articles.body: I run a visa agency in Bali. The other half of my week goes into Apify Actors, and one of them reads Trip.com: a city, two dates and a guest count in, one row per hotel out, with the live nightly rate for exactly those dates. Trip.com is the booking channel for most of Asia and it has no public web API, so a scraper is the only way in. The field I expected to cause trouble was the price. It didn't. What caused trouble was something I hadn't thought to check: which hotels the page shows you at all. The same URL, five times, one day My QA runs hit a hardcoded list URL so I can diff the output day over day.

articles.title: The UK Treasury is asking whether bank APIs should stay free. Do the maths now.
articles.excerpt: Every open banking pitch has a line in it that nobody reads twice: the bank APIs are free. That's true today. It's also the biggest assumption in most open banking business plans, and HM Treasury has…
articles.body: Every open banking pitch has a line in it that nobody reads twice: the bank APIs are free. That's true today. It's also the biggest assumption in most open banking business plans, and HM Treasury has now asked, in writing, whether it should stay true. What the Treasury actually said In July, HM Treasury put out a consultation on modernising the Payment Services Regulations. It closed on 6 October. The open banking bits, as I read them: A new statutory right of access for VRPs. A worry that free access gives banks little reason to invest in their APIs. FCA oversight of open banking pricing, with the door open to charging for some kinds of access. A future framework where the FCA has a say over standards, participation, pricing, funding and disputes.

articles.body: Built for the TestSprite Hackathon, Season 4. Live: tera-orpin-three.vercel.app · Code: github.com/PugarHuda/tera Founders are afraid to touch pricing, and they are right to be. Move a customer from $29 to $79 on day 17 of a 31-day month and Stripe writes two proration lines you have probably never computed by hand: an "Unused time" credit of −$14.03 and a "Remaining time" charge of $38.23, on top of the $79 renewal. Add a coupon that was applied once, a tax rate that is inclusive, a trial, or a subscription in Stripe's new flexible billing mode, and the invoice your customer sees is no longer something you can predict from the pricing page. Tera simulates it first.

articles.title: One leaking FFmpeg process took down six live streams
articles.excerpt: A live event cannot be restarted. When we built Bunryu, aself-hosted server that forwards one live stream to many destinations, we assumed things would go wrong and tried to keep each failure small. I…
articles.body: A live event cannot be restarted. When we built Bunryu , aself-hosted server that forwards one live stream to many destinations, we assumed things would go wrong and tried to keep each failure small. In July 2026 a single FFmpeg process showed us where that was not true yet. The question Someone looked at the dashboard and asked: "Output 1 has an error, output 2 doesn't. Why?" Output 1's last error was exit=SIGKILL . That is not an application error, so we went to the host logs. What happened Six streams were running on one VM, with three pipelines and six outputs. This is the chain we pieced together from the logs: All six encoders dropped and reconnected repeatedly for about eleven minutes. When the streams settled, every output's FFmpeg process restarted and resynchronised.

articles.title: A Practical Prompt Framework for Consistent Halloween Photo-to-Video Results
articles.excerpt: Photo-to-video generation looks simple: upload a portrait, describe a transformation, and wait for the result. In practice, short transformation clips often fail in predictable ways. Faces drift, the…
articles.body: Photo-to-video generation looks simple: upload a portrait, describe a transformation, and wait for the result. In practice, short transformation clips often fail in predictable ways. Faces drift, the effect starts too early, the camera moves for no reason, or the final frame becomes a completely different person. After working on a small Halloween photo-to-video project, I found that better results come less from adding adjectives and more from giving the model a clear sequence of constraints. This post explains the prompt structure I now use for seasonal transformation videos. The example is a glowing pumpkin-head reveal, but the framework also works for costumes, fantasy makeovers, pet transformations, and other short visual effects.

articles.body: Dear NASA Science Community, NASA Science wants to deliver science faster, so we’re changing how we compete and select missions. On Monday, October 26, we will host a virtual NASA Science Town Hall, from NASA Headquarters, to explain our new Competition Model 2.0 (CM 2.0), and answer your questions. We have heard you. We have listened. We know that the burden of bringing great ideas forward has been too heavy for too long. It has taken years to move mission concepts through the current two-step process. articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 21, 2008: India launches its 1st mission to the moon with Chandrayaan-1
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor. Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. (Launch occurred at 8:52 p.m. EDT, though it was about 6:22 a.m. local time at the launch site on Oct. 22.) It arrived in lunar orbit about three weeks later and dropped off the Moon Impact Probe, which crashed into the moon on Nov. 14. The rest of the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft stayed in orbit, where it collected and transmitted data from the moon to Earth for about a year.
